translations.text: Next we append the First Book of Ezra. This is according to the version of the Seventy.
Josiah celebrated the Passover in Jerusalem for his Lord, and he slaughtered the Passover offerings on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He appointed the priests to the service of their assigned days, clothed in robes in the house of the Lord.

And they said to the Levites, the priests, the men of Israel, “Consecrate yourselves to the Lord at the placing of the Lord’s holy ark, and put the holy ark in the house that King Solomon, David’s son, built.”

And Josiah said, “You no longer need to carry it on your shoulders. Now, therefore, serve the Lord your God and give relief to his people Israel. Prepare the house according to your clans and your appointed days of service, according to the writing of David king of Israel and the directions given by his son King Solomon.

Stand in the sanctuary according to the divisions of your ancestral households, you Levites who stand before your brothers, the Israelites, with each portion of the Levites’ ancestral households in its proper order.
Slaughter the Passover as sacrifices. Prepare it for your brothers, and celebrate the Passover according to the Lord’s commandment that was given to Moses.”

Josiah contributed to the people who were present thirty thousand sheep, lambs, and young goats for the Passover, and three thousand bulls. These animals were given from the king’s possessions. His chief official also contributed to the people, the priests, and the Levites.
Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Hazael, the leaders of the house of God, gave to the priests. For the Passover they gave two thousand six hundred sheep, lambs, and young goats, and three hundred bulls.
Benaiah, Shemaiah, his brother Nethanel, Hashkiah, Jehiel, and Jozabar, the leaders of the Levites, contributed to the Levites a thousand sheep and seven hundred bulls for the Passover.

When these things had been properly arranged, the priests and Levites took their places appropriately, with unleavened bread, according to their clans and the leadership of their ancestral divisions, before the people, to make offerings to the Lord according to what is written in the book of Moses. And so it was in the morning.
They roasted the Passover over fire as required, and boiled the sacrifices in cauldrons and pots with a pleasant aroma, and brought them to all the people.
After these things, they also made preparations for themselves and for their brothers the priests, the descendants of Aaron.
For the priests were offering up the fat until night, and the Levites prepared portions for themselves and for their brothers the priests, the descendants of Aaron.
The priestly singers, the descendants of Asaph, were in their assigned places according to the arrangements made by David, Asaph, Zechariah, and Eddinus, who belonged to the royal household.
The gatekeepers were at each of the gateways. None of them needed to leave his appointed daily service, because their brothers the Levites prepared portions for them.
The arrangements for the Lord’s sacrifice were completed that day, to celebrate the Passover and offer sacrifices before the Lord’s altar, according to King Josiah’s command.
The Israelites who were present at that time celebrated the Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
No Passover like this had been celebrated in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet.
None of the kings of Israel had celebrated a Passover like the one celebrated by Josiah, the priests, the Levites, the Judeans, and all Israel who were present in their royal capital, Jerusalem.
This Passover took place in the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign.
And Josiah’s deeds were upright before his Lord, with a heart full of reverent devotion.

The things concerning him are written in the accounts of former times, concerning those who sinned and acted wickedly against the Lord more than any other people or kingdom, and those who knowingly distressed him. And the words of the Lord stood against Israel.
After all these deeds of Josiah, Pharaoh king of Egypt came to wage war at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.
The king of Egypt sent word to him, saying, “What have I to do with you, king of Judah?
“I have not been sent against you by the Lord God, for my war is on the Euphrates. Now the Lord is with me. Withdraw, and do not oppose the Lord.”
Josiah did not turn back in his chariot, but sought to fight against him, paying no attention to the words of Jeremiah the prophet, which came from the Lord’s mouth.
Instead, he engaged him in battle in the plain of Megiddo, and the commanders came down against King Josiah.
The king said to his servants, “Take me away from the fighting, for I have become very weak.” His servants immediately took him away from the battle line.
He mounted his second chariot, and when he returned to Jerusalem, he departed this life and was buried in his ancestral tomb.

Throughout Judah they mourned Josiah, and Jeremiah the prophet lamented over Josiah. Those who sat in the foremost places, together with their wives, continued to lament him to this day. This was established as a permanent practice throughout the whole people of Israel.

These things are written in the book of the histories of the kings of Judah: every event concerning Josiah’s deeds, his renown, and his understanding of the Lord’s law. His earlier deeds and his more recent ones are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
The people took Jehoahaz, Josiah’s son, and proclaimed him king in place of his father Josiah, when he was twenty-three years old.
He reigned over Israel and in Jerusalem for three months, and the king of Egypt removed him from reigning in Jerusalem.
He exacted from the people a hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
The king of Egypt appointed his brother Jehoiakim king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Jehoiakim imprisoned the nobles, and he seized his brother Zahrion and brought him up from Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king over Judah in Jerusalem, and he did what was evil before the Lord.
Afterward Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came up, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also took some of the Lord’s sacred vessels, carried them away, and placed them in his temple in Babylon.
The things recorded about him, his uncleanness, and his evil wickedness are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings.
His son Jehoiakim became king in his place, for when he was presented, he was eight years old.
He reigned in Jerusalem for three months and ten days, and did what was evil before the Lord.
After a year, Nebuchadnezzar sent and had him taken to Babylon, together with the Lord’s sacred vessels.
He appointed Zedekiah king of Judah and Jerusalem when he was twenty-one years old, and he reigned for eleven years.
He did what was evil before the Lord and felt no shame before the words spoken by Jeremiah the prophet from the mouth of the Lord.

Although Nebuchadnezzar had made him swear an oath in the Lord's name, he broke his oaths and turned away. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart, transgressing the laws of the Lord, the God of Israel.

The leaders of the people and of the priests committed many wicked and unjust acts, exceeding all the abominations of all the nations. They defiled the Lord's temple, which had been consecrated in Jerusalem.
The God of their ancestors sent word through his messenger to bring them back, because he had compassion on them and on his dwelling place.

But they mocked his messenger, and on the day when the Lord spoke, they were ridiculing his prophets, until he became angry with his people because of their evil wickedness and commanded the kings of the Chaldeans to come up against them.
They killed their young men with the sword in the precincts of his holy temple. He had no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or child, but handed them all over to them.
They took all the Lord's sacred vessels, large and small, the Lord's ark, and the royal treasuries, and carried them to Babylon.
They burned the house of the Lord, tore down the walls of Jerusalem, and burned its palaces with fire.
They completely destroyed all its splendid things and led those who remained away to Babylon at swordpoint.
They were slaves to him and to his sons until the Persians came to power, fulfilling the Lord's word spoken through Jeremiah.
Until the land had enjoyed its Sabbaths, it would rest throughout the whole time of its desolation, to complete seventy years.
In the first year of the reign of Cyrus king of the Persians, to fulfill the Lord's word spoken through Jeremiah,
the Lord stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he issued a proclamation throughout his entire kingdom, also putting it in writing, saying:
“This is what Cyrus king of the Persians says: The Lord of Israel, the Lord Most High, has appointed me king of the inhabited world.
and has instructed me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
Whoever among you belongs to his people, may his Lord be with him. Let him go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the Lord of Israel. He is the Lord who dwells in Jerusalem.

Therefore, wherever any of them lives, let the people of his locality help him with gold and silver, with gifts, with horses and livestock, along with the other things added as votive offerings to the Lord's temple in Jerusalem.”

Then the heads of the tribe of the family of Judah and of the tribe of Benjamin, the priests, the Levites, and all those whose spirits the Lord had stirred arose to go up and build a house for the Lord in Jerusalem.
Those around them helped with everything: silver and gold, horses and livestock, and many votive offerings from the many whose hearts were moved.
King Cyrus brought out the Lord's sacred vessels, which Nebuchadnezzar had removed from Jerusalem and placed in his temple of Persian idols.
He handed them over to Mithridates, his treasurer.
Through him they were handed over to Shalmaneser, the governor of Judah.
Their number was as follows: a thousand gold cups, twenty-nine silver plates, thirty gold bowls, two thousand four hundred and ten silver bowls, and a thousand other vessels.
All the gold and silver vessels that were taken numbered five thousand four hundred and sixty-nine.
They went up from Shalmaneser with the captives from Babylon to Jerusalem.

In the time of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, Belemus, Mithridates, Tullius, Rathumus, Beeltethmus, Samellius the scribe, and the others associated with them, who lived in Samaria and other places, wrote against those living in Judah and Jerusalem the following letter:
“To King Artaxerxes our lord, from your servants Rathumus, the official in charge of affairs, Samellius the scribe, the other members of their council, and the judges in Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

And now let our lord the king know that the Jews who came up from you and arrived here among us in Jerusalem are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city. They are repairing its streets and walls and laying the foundations of a very lofty temple.

If, then, this city is rebuilt and its walls are completed, they will not submit to paying tribute, but will rise against the kings. Since these things concerning the temple are being done, we think it right not to overlook such a matter, but to tell our lord the king, so that, if it seems good to you, a search may be made in these records inherited from your ancestors.

You will find in the archives the things written about this, and you will learn that this city was rebellious and caused trouble for kings and cities. The Jews are rebels, gathered in it and engaged in warfare since ancient times [?]. It was for this reason that this city was destroyed.
Now, therefore, we inform you, our lord the king, that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are erected, you will no longer have access to Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

Then the king wrote in reply to Rathumus, who had recorded these events, to Beeltethmus, to Semellius the scribe, and to the rest of their associates living in Samaria, Syria, and Phoenicia, as written below:
I have read the letter you sent me. I therefore ordered a search, and I found that this city has acted against kings since ancient times.
Its people carry out rebellions and wars within it. There were powerful and harsh kings in Jerusalem who ruled over Coele-Syria and Phoenicia and collected tribute from them.

Now, therefore, I have ordered those people to be stopped from rebuilding the city, and care to be taken that nothing be done beyond these orders, so that these evils do not spread further and cause trouble for the kings.

Then, when the things written by King Artaxerxes were read, Rathumus, Semellius the scribe, and their associates hurried back to Jerusalem with horses and a crowd. They immediately began stopping those who were building. The construction of the temple in Jerusalem remained suspended until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of the Persians.
King Darius gave a great banquet for all those under him, all those born in his household, and all the nobles of Media and Persia,
and for all the satraps, generals, and local governors under him, from India to Cush, in the 127 satrapies.
They ate and drank, and when they had eaten their fill, they went home. King Darius himself went back to his bedroom, slept, and woke up.
Then three young men, the bodyguards who guarded the king's person, said to one another,
“Let each of us make a statement about what is strongest. To the one whose statement is judged wiser than his companion's, King Darius will give great gifts and great rewards for victory:
purple robes to wear, a gold cup to drink from, a gold bed to sleep on, a gold chariot to ride in, a fine linen turban, and a necklace for his neck.”
“He will sit next to Darius because of his wisdom and will be called a relative of Darius.”
Then each wrote down his own statement, and they sealed them and placed them beneath King Darius's pillows. They said,
“When the king wakes up, they will give him the document. Whoever's statement the king and the three nobles of Persia judge to be wisest will receive the reward for victory, as written.”
So they wrote, one by one: “Wine is strongest.”
Another wrote: “The king is strongest.”
The third wrote: “Women are strongest, but truth prevails over everything.”
When the king woke up, they took the document, gave it to him, and he read it.
He sent for all the nobles of Persia and Media, the satraps, generals, local governors, and chief officials. They sat in the audience hall, and the document was read before them.
They said, “Call the young men, and let them explain their statements.” They were called and came in.
They said to them, “Explain to us what you have written.” The first, who had spoken about the strength of wine, began and said:
“Gentlemen, is not wine stronger than all human beings? It leads astray the minds of those who drink it.
“It makes the mind of the king and the orphan the same, and likewise those of the household servant, the freeborn, the poor, and the rich.
“It changes every mind to pleasure and joy, and a person forgets every sorrow and every debt.
It makes every heart rich, and neither king nor satrap is remembered. It makes them speak of everything in terms of talents [?].
“When people drink, they forget to love their friends and brothers, and before long they draw their swords.
“When they recover from the wine, they do not remember what they have done.
“Gentlemen, is wine not strongest, since it compels people to act this way?” When he had said this, he fell silent.
The second, who had spoken about the king’s strength, began to speak:
“Gentlemen, are not human beings stronger? They control the land and the sea and everything in them.
But the mighty king rules over them and is their master. Whatever he tells them, they obey.
If he tells them to fight one another, they do so. If he sends them against enemies, they go and break through mountains, walls, and fortresses.
They kill and are killed, but they do not disobey the king's command. If they win, they bring everything to the king, including whatever they plunder and all the other things.
All those who do not serve as soldiers or fight, but cultivate the land, also bring the king what they harvest from what they sow. They press one another to bring tribute to the king.
He is only one man. If he orders them to kill, they kill; if he orders them to spare, they spare.
If he orders them to strike, they strike; if he orders them to destroy, they destroy; if he orders them to build, they build.
If he orders them to cut down, they cut down; if he orders them to plant, they plant.
All his people and his armies obey him. Yet while all this happens, he reclines, eating, drinking, and sleeping.
These men stand guard beside him, and none of them can go away to attend to his own affairs, nor do they disobey him.
“Men, is not the king more powerful, since he is obeyed like this?” And he fell silent.
Then the third man, who had spoken about women and truth—Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah—began to speak.
“Gentlemen, is not the king great, are not human beings numerous, and is not wine powerful? Who, then, overcomes them, or who rules over them?
Is it not women who give birth to kings and to all the people who rule over sea and land?
They came from women, and women raise those who planted the vineyards from which wine comes.
Women make men's clothes, and they bring men honor. Men cannot exist apart from women.
But if men gather gold and silver and every beautiful thing, and then see a woman who is lovely in appearance and beauty,
they leave all these things behind and are astonished at her. They stare at her with their mouths open, and they all love her more than gold, silver, or any beautiful thing.
A man leaves his own father, who raised him, and his own country, and clings to his wife.
He gives himself over to his wife and remembers neither father nor mother nor country.
From this you ought to recognize that women rule over you. Do you not labor and grow weary, and give and bring everything to women?
A man takes a sword in his hand to go traveling, robbing, and stealing, and to sail on the sea and on rivers.
He faces a lion and walks in darkness, and whatever he steals, seizes, and plunders, he brings to his beloved.
A man loves a woman far more than his father and mother.
Many have lost their minds because of women and have become slaves because of them.
Many have perished, become bewildered, and gone astray because of women.
And now, do you not believe me? Is not the king great in his authority? Are not all lands afraid to touch him?
I saw him with Apame, the daughter of the great Artax, that renowned man, who was the king's concubine.
She was lifting the crown from his head and putting it on herself, and striking the king on his left side.
Yet despite all this, the king stared at her with his mouth open. If she laughed at him, he laughed. But if she became bitter toward him, he kept troubling her so that she would be reconciled to him.
Men, how can women not be powerful, when they do such things?
Then the king and the nobles looked at one another and began to speak about truth.
Gentlemen, are not women powerful? The earth is great, heaven is high, and the sun is swift in its course, for it circles around heaven and runs back to its own place in a single day.
Is not the one who made these things great? And truth is great and far more powerful than everything.
The whole earth calls upon truth, and heaven blesses it. All works shake and tremble, and there is no injustice whatsoever in it.
The king is unjust, women are unjust, all human beings are unjust, and all their deeds are unjust—all things of this kind. There is no truth in them, and they perish in their injustice.
But truth stands firm and is powerful forever, and holds sway forever and ever.
With truth there is no favoritism or partiality. Instead, it does what is just, unlike all those who are unjust and evil, and everyone finds pleasure in its deeds.
There is no injustice whatsoever in its judgment. To it belong power, kingship, authority, and greatness over all nations. Blessed is the God of truth!”
He stopped speaking, and then all the people cried out, saying, “Truth is great and more powerful!”
Then the king said to him, “Ask for whatever you wish, beyond what is written, and it will be given to you, since you have proved to be the wisest. You shall sit beside me and be called my kinsman.”
Then he said to the king, “Remember the vow you made to rebuild Jerusalem on the day when you received your crown,
and to send back all the vessels taken from Jerusalem, which Cyrus had set apart when he vowed to send them there.
You vowed to build there the temple that the Edomites burned when Judah was devastated by the Chaldeans.

And now this is what I implore you to do, my lord the king, and what I ask of you. This, then, is the honor I seek from you: that you fulfill the vow you made with your own mouth to the King of heaven.”

Then King Darius stood up and kissed him. He wrote letters for him to all the administrators, district governors, military commanders, and satraps, instructing them to escort him and all those with him who were going up to rebuild Jerusalem.

He also wrote letters to all the district governors in Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, and to those in Lebanon, instructing them to transport cedar timber from Lebanon to Jerusalem and to help him build the city.
He wrote concerning the freedom of all the Jews going up from the kingdom to Judea, declaring that no ruler, satrap, district governor, or administrator should come to their gates.
Every territory they held was to be theirs without taxation, and the Edomites were to give up the villages they held that belonged to the Jews.
Twenty talents of silver were to be given every year for the construction of the temple until it was built.
They were to offer whole burnt offerings on the altar every day, as they had been commanded to offer, and an additional ten talents every year.
All those setting out from Babylon to build the city were to have freedom, both they and their children, as were all the priests who were setting out.
He also wrote instructions for providing necessities and the priestly robe in which they ministered.
And he wrote that the Levites were to be supplied with what they needed until the temple was completed and Jerusalem was rebuilt.
He wrote instructions that all those guarding the city should be given allotments and provisions.
And he sent all the vessels that King Cyrus had set apart from Babylon. Everything that Cyrus had said should be done, he too ordered to be done and sent to Jerusalem.
Then that young man went out, and, lifting his face toward heaven in the direction of Jerusalem, he blessed the King of heaven, saying:
“Victory comes from you, and wisdom comes from you. Yours is the glory, and I am a member of your household.
Blessed are you, who have given me wisdom. I thank you, Lord of our ancestors.”
He took the letters, departed, and came to Babylon, where he informed all his brothers.
And they blessed the God of their ancestors because he had given them rest and release,
to go up and rebuild Jerusalem and the temple over which his name had been proclaimed. And they drank with music and rejoicing for seven days.
After this, the heads of the ancestral families were chosen to go up according to their tribes, together with their wives, sons, daughters, male and female slaves, and livestock.
And Darius sent a thousand horsemen with them to bring them safely to Jerusalem, with music, [?], and pipes.
All their brothers were making merry, and he had them go up together with them.
These are the names of the men who were going up, according to their leadership:

The priests, descendants of Phinehas son of Aaron: [?], son of Jozadak, son of Seraiah, and Joiakim, son of Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, from the house of David, of the family of Perez and the tribe of Judah.
He was the one who spoke wise words before Darius king of the Persians in the second year of his reign, in Nisan, the first month.
These are the people from Judah who came up from captivity, from their exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported to Babylon.

They returned to Jerusalem and the rest of Judah, each to his own town. These came with Zerubbabel and Jeshua: Nehemiah, Zerahiah, Reesaiah, Hananiah, Mordecai, Beelsarus, Aspharasu, Borealiah, Roim, and Baanah, their leaders.
The number of those from the people and their leaders: the descendants of Perez, 2,172; the descendants of Shaphat, 372.
the descendants of Arush, 756;
the descendants of Phali, the leader of Moab and son of Jeshua and Hobad, 1,802;
The descendants of Jolaham, two; the descendants of Azatu, 970; the descendants of Corbe, 633; the descendants of Bani, 648.
the descendants of Bebai, 705; the descendants of Argu, 1,322;
The descendants of Adonikam, thirty-seven; the descendants of Baasha, 2,606; the descendants of Asahel, 454.
And Nehemiah said to them, “You must not share in the holy offerings until a high priest arises wearing the Urim and Thummim.”
All those of Israel aged twelve and above, apart from male and female slaves, numbered 42,460. Their male and female slaves numbered 7,337; singers and musicians, 245.
Camels, 435; horses, 7,036; mules, 245; donkeys, 5,525.
And some of the heads of the families, when they came to the temple of God in Jerusalem, vowed to set up the house on its own site, their temple.
And for the priestly treasury for the work: a thousand minas of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and a hundred priestly robes.
The priests, the Levites, and those of his people settled in Jerusalem and the surrounding country; the priestly singers, the gatekeepers, and all Israel settled in their villages.
When the seventh month began, while the Israelites were each in their own places, they gathered together in the square at the first gate, the one toward the east.
Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, together with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his kinsmen, arose and prepared the altar of God,
to offer whole burnt offerings on it in accordance with what is stated in the book of Moses, the man of God.

And they all gathered from among the other peoples of the land and set up the altar on its site, because all the peoples in the land were hostile to them. They took courage and offered sacrifices at the appointed times and whole burnt offerings to the Lord in the morning and evening.
And they celebrated the Festival of Booths as commanded in the law, with sacrifices each day as required.
And after these, the regular offerings and the sacrifices for the Sabbaths, the new moons, and all the sacred festivals.
And all those who had made a vow to God began offering sacrifices to God from the new moon of the seventh month, although the temple of God had not yet been built.

They gave money to the stonecutters and carpenters, and drink, food, and provisions for celebration to the Sidonians and Tyrians, to bring them cedar timber from Lebanon and transport it on rafts to the harbor of Joppa, according to the decree that King Cyrus had issued in writing for them.

In the second year, when he came to the temple of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak began, together with their brothers, the priests and Levites, and all those who had come from captivity to Jerusalem.
They laid the foundation of the temple of God on the new moon of the second month of the second year after they came to Judah and Jerusalem.

They appointed the Levites aged twenty and older to oversee the Lord’s work. Jeshua, his sons and brothers, and Zamuel his brother, and the sons of Jeshua, Amadabun, and the sons of Judah, and Eliada with his sons and brothers—all Levites—together supervised the workers engaged in the work at the Lord’s house. And the builders built the Lord’s temple.
The priests stood dressed in robes, with musical instruments and trumpets, and the Levites, the descendants of Asaph, had cymbals, praising and blessing the Lord according to David king of Israel.
They cried out in songs of praise, blessing the Lord because his goodness and praise are forever over all Israel.
All the people cheered and shouted loudly, praising the Lord because the Lord’s house was being established.

Some of the priests and Levites and the heads of the households, according to their clans—the old men who had seen the house that stood before this one—came to the construction of this house with shouting and great weeping.
And many others sounded trumpets and rejoiced loudly.
The people could not hear the trumpets because of the people’s weeping, for the assembly was crying out so loudly that it could be heard from far away.
When the enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard it, they came to find out what the sound of the trumpets meant.
They learned that those who had returned from captivity were building a temple for the Lord, the God of Israel.
They approached Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the leaders of the tribes and said to them, “Let us build with you.
“For, like you, we obey your Lord, and we have sacrificed to him since the days of Ashtakpath, king of the Assyrians, who brought us here.”
Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the heads of the tribes of Israel said to them, “It is not for us and you together to build a house for the Lord our God.
For we alone will build for the Lord our God, the God of Israel, in accordance with what Cyrus king of the Persians commanded us.”
But the peoples of the land who were arrayed against those in Judah and were hemming them in through warfare prevented them from building.

By making plans, bringing in people, and holding assemblies, they prevented them from building and completing the construction throughout the lifetime of King Cyrus. They were kept from building for two years, until the reign of Darius.
The prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, who was over them.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began building the house of God in Jerusalem, with the Lord’s prophets there helping them.
At that time Sisinnes, the governor of Syria and Phoenicia, and Sathrabuzanes and their associates approached them and said to them:
“Who commanded you to build this house and complete this roof and all these other things? And who are the builders who are completing these things?”
The elders of the Jews found favor when the Lord showed care for the exiles.
They were not prevented from building until Darius was informed about them and a report was made to him.

A copy of the letter they wrote to Darius and sent: Sisinnes, the governor of Syria and Phoenicia, and Sathrabuzanes and their associates, the officials in Syria and Phoenicia, to King Darius, greetings.

Let all these things be known to our lord the king: when we came to the territory of Judah and entered the city of Jerusalem, we found the elders of the Jewish exiles in the city of Jerusalem building a great new house for the Lord with costly cut stones and timber being placed in the buildings.
The work was being done diligently, and it was prospering in their hands and being diligently completed in all its splendor.
Then we questioned those elders, saying, “Who commanded you to build this house and lay the foundations for this work?”
We therefore questioned them so that we could inform you and write to you about their leading men. We asked them for a written list of the names of the foremost of their leaders.
They answered us, saying, “We are servants of the Lord who created heaven and earth.
The house had been built many years before by a great and powerful king of Israel, and it had been completed.
And because our ancestors sinned against the heavenly Lord of Israel by provoking him, he handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of the Chaldeans.
They demolished and burned the house and took the people captive to Babylon.
But in the first year, when Cyrus was king, [?] to build this house.

The gold and silver sacred vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem and placed in his own temple—King Cyrus brought these out again from the temple in Babylon, and they were handed over to Zerubbabel and Sheshbazzar the governor.
He was given instructions, and he brought all these vessels to be placed in the temple in Jerusalem. The Lord’s temple was to be rebuilt on its original site.
Then Sheshbazzar, after arriving, laid the foundations of the Lord’s house in Jerusalem. From that time until now it has been under construction and has not been completed.
Now therefore, if you consider it right, O king, let a search be made in the archive of the royal records of King Cyrus in Babylon.

If you find that the construction of the Lord’s house in Jerusalem was undertaken by order of King Cyrus, and if our lord the king considers it right, let him send us a response concerning these matters.

Then King Darius ordered a search of the archive of the records deposited in Babylon. At Ecbatana, in the citadel in the land of Media, a passage was found in which the following things were recorded:
In the first year of King Cyrus’s reign, Cyrus ordered that the Lord’s house in Jerusalem be rebuilt, where sacrifices are continually offered by fire.

Its height is to be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits, with three courses of cut stone and one course of new timber from the country itself. The expenses are to be paid from the treasury of King Cyrus.

The gold and silver sacred vessels of the Lord’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the house in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, are to be returned to the house in Jerusalem, where they had previously been kept, so that they may be placed there.

He also ordered Sisinnes, governor of Syria and Phoenicia, Sathrabuzanes, their associates, and the officials appointed in Syria and Phoenicia to take care to keep away from the site. They were to allow Zerubbabel, the Lord’s servant and governor of Judea, and the elders of the Jews to build that house on its site.
I too have ordered that it be rebuilt completely and that care be taken to assist the exiles from Judea until the Lord’s house is completed.
From the tribute of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, an allowance is to be provided diligently to those men, to Zerubbabel the governor, for bulls, rams, and lambs for sacrifice to the Lord.
Likewise, wheat, salt, wine, and oil are to be supplied continually every year, according to what the priests in Jerusalem report is used each day, without question.
This is so that drink offerings may be presented to the Most High God on behalf of the king and his servants, and that they may pray for their lives.

You shall also order that, if anyone violates anything that is written or attempts to nullify it, a timber is to be taken from his property and he is to be hanged on it, and his possessions are to become royal property.
Because of these things, may the Lord, who has proclaimed his name there, bring ruin on every king and people who stretches out a hand to hinder or harm the Lord’s house in Jerusalem.
I, King Darius, have expressly commanded that these things be done.
Then Sisinnes, governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, Sathrabuzanes, and their associates complied with the orders given by King Darius.
They supervised the sacred work, very diligently assisting the elders of the Jews and the officials responsible for the sacred service.
The sacred work prospered while the prophets Haggai and Zechariah prophesied.
They completed these things by the command of the Lord, the God of Israel, and by the orders of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia.
By the sixth year of Darius king of Persia, the holy house was completed, by the twenty-third day of the month of Adar in the sixth year of King Darius.
The Israelites, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of those from the captivity who had joined them acted in accordance with what is in the book of Moses.
For the dedication of the Lord’s temple, they offered one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs,
Twelve male goats for the sins of all Israel, corresponding to the number of the twelve tribal leaders of Israel.
The priests and Levites, clothed in robes, took their places by their families for the service of the Lord, the God of Israel, in accordance with the book of Moses, with gatekeepers at each gate.
The Israelites who had returned from captivity celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, because the priests and Levites had purified themselves together.
Not all those who had returned from captivity had purified themselves, but all the Levites had purified themselves together.
They slaughtered the Passover sacrifice for all those who had returned from captivity, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.
The Israelites who had returned from captivity ate, along with all those who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land and were seeking the Lord.
They celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days, rejoicing before the Lord.
For he had changed the attitude of the king of the Assyrians toward them, strengthening their hands for the work of the Lord, the God of Israel.
After these things [?], while Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, was reigning, Ezra came up. He was of the family of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum,

son of Zadok, son of Ahitub, son of Amariah, son of Uzziah, son of Meremoth, son of Zerah, son of Shaviah, son of Bukki, son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, the first priest.
This Ezra came up from Babylon, being a scribe skilled in the law of Moses, which had been given by the God of Israel.
The king honored him, since he had found favor with him in all his requests.
Some of the Israelites, priests, Levites, priestly singers, gatekeepers, and servants of the priests went up with him to Jerusalem,

in the seventh year of Artaxerxes' reign, in the fifth month. This was the king's seventh year. They left Babylon on the first day of the first month and arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, in keeping with the success granted them by the Lord [?].
For he [?] possessed great knowledge, so that he would leave out nothing from the Lord's law and commandments, and would also teach all Israel the statutes and judgments.
Now the decree came which King Artaxerxes had written to Ezra, the priest and reader of the Lord's law. Its text is set down here:
King Artaxerxes to Ezra, the priest and reader of the law of the Lord: Greetings.
I have decided on these acts of kindness and have ordered those of the Jewish people who ask and are willing, and those of the priests and Levites who are in our kingdom, to go with you to Jerusalem,
All those, therefore, who intend to go shall depart, as seemed good to me and to the seven friends and counselors,
so that they may attend to the affairs of Judah and Jerusalem in accordance with what is in the Lord's law,

and bring to Jerusalem the offerings to the Lord which I and my friends have vowed, together with all the gold and silver that may be found in the region of Babylon for the Lord in Jerusalem, along with what has been offered by the people for the temple of their Lord in Jerusalem.
to collect gold and silver for bulls, rams, and lambs, and for the things that accompany them,
so that sacrifices may be offered on the altar of their Lord in Jerusalem.
Whatever you and your brothers wish to do with the gold and silver, carry it out according to the will of your God.
And the Lord's sacred vessels, which are being given for the use of the temple of your God in Jerusalem, and whatever other things you may need for the use of the temple of your God.
you shall provide from the royal treasury.

I, King Artaxerxes, have also commanded the treasury officials of Syria and Phoenicia to give Ezra, the priest and reader of the law of God Most High, whatever he sends for, taking care to provide it, up to a hundred talents of silver.
and likewise up to one hundred kors of wheat, one hundred measures of wine, and other things.
These things are to be carried out for God Most High according to God's law, so that wrath may not come upon the kingdom of the king and his sons.

You are also informed that no tax or other levy is to be imposed on any of the priests, Levites, priestly singers, gatekeepers, servants of the priests, or scribes of this temple. No one is to have authority to impose these on them.
And you, Ezra, in accordance with God's wisdom, appoint judges and magistrates to judge throughout Syria and Phoenicia all those who transgress the law of your God. Teach those who do not know it.
All those who transgress the law of your God and the royal law are to be duly punished, whether by death, corporal punishment, a monetary penalty, or banishment.
Ezra the scribe said, “Blessed be the Lord alone, who put these things into the king's heart, to bring glory to his house in Jerusalem.
and who honored me before the king, those who advise him, and all his friends and nobles.
I took great courage through the help of the Lord my God, and I gathered men from Israel to go up with me.
These are the principal leaders according to their families, and the heads of the divisions who went up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes:
From the descendants of Parosh: Tarosh, son of Tamush. From the descendants of Ataroth: Gamalusi. From the descendants of David.
Perez [?], Zechariah, and with him, according to the register, 150 men.
From the descendants of Maath-moab [?]: Elhanan son of Zerah, and with him 200 men.
From the descendants of Zattu: Jeconiah, son of Athilu, and with him two hundred men. From the descendants of Adinobin: Nunthan, and with him two hundred and fifty men.
From the descendants of Lemaasiah [?]: Athaliah, and with him 270 men.
From the descendants of Shephatiah: Zerana [?], of Michael, and with him 70 men.
From the descendants of Joab: Obadiah son of Hezekiel, and with him 212 men.
From the men of [?], Shelomith, son of Josiphiah, and with him 160 men.
From the descendants of Becher: Zechariah of Bebel, and with him twenty-eight men.
From the descendants of Ashdoth: John son of Akta, and with him one hundred and ten men.
From the descendants of Adonikam, those who came last, whose names were Eliphelet, son of Galul, and Shemaiah, and with them seventy men.
And from the descendants of Bani: the one in Ekron, and with him seventy men.
I gathered them at the river called Taeran, and we camped there for three days, and I inspected them.
But I found none of the priests or Levites there.
I sent for Eleazar, and when he came, Agon, Maasman, Saltan, Shemaiah, Nuriban, Nethanan, Taantan, Zechariah, and Moshiah [?], from among the leaders and knowledgeable men.
I told them to go to Ladan, the leader who was at the place where the treasury was kept.
I instructed them to speak to Laadan and his brothers, and to those at the place where the treasury was guarded, to send us men who would minister in the house of our Lord.
Through the supporting hand of the Lord our God, he brought us knowledgeable men from the descendants of Mahli, the Levite of Israel: Shabkiah, with his sons and brothers, eighteen in all.
Also Hashabiah, Hanuna, and Aatan, from among the brothers of the descendants of Canaan, and their sons, twenty men.
And from the temple servants whom David and the leaders had assigned to the service of the Levites, there were two hundred and twenty temple servants, all of whose names I had recorded in writing.
There I vowed a fast, [?], before the Lord our God,
to ask him for success for us and for the children and livestock that were with us.
For I had refrained from asking the king for cavalry and infantry as an escort, to protect us against those who opposed us.
For we had told the king, “The power of the Lord our God is with those who seek him in complete uprightness.”
And concerning all these things [?], we again pleaded before the Lord our God, and we were granted forgiveness.
I selected twelve distinguished men from the heads of the priestly families, and Shemaiah, and with them ten men from among their brothers.
I weighed out for them the silver, the gold, and the sacred vessels for the house of our Lord, which the king, his counselors, the nobles, and all Israel had donated.

I weighed out and entrusted to them [?] six hundred and fifty talents of silver, silver vessels weighing one hundred talents, one hundred talents of gold, twenty gold vessels, and twelve bronze vessels made of fine, shining bronze.
I said to them, “You yourselves are holy to the Lord, and the vessels are holy. The gold and silver are an offering vowed to the Lord, the God of your ancestors.
Be watchful and guard them until you hand them over to the priestly and Levitical families and the heads of Israel’s families in Jerusalem, in the treasury of the house of our Lord.”
The priests and Levites who received the silver, gold, and vessels brought them into the Lord’s temple in Jerusalem.

We set out from the river Taertha on the twelfth day of the first month and came to Jerusalem through the supporting hand of the Lord our God, which was over us. It delivered us from attacks by every enemy, and we came to Jerusalem.
After we had been there for three days, on the fourth day the silver and gold were weighed and handed over in the house of the Lord our God to Anremoth son of Uriah the priest.
With him was Eleazar, the son of Phinehas. With them were Jobad, Jeshua son of Mahud, of Abnu, the Levite [?]. Everything was accounted for by number and weight, the entire weight at that very time.

Those who had returned from captivity offered sacrifices to the God of Israel: ninety-six lambs, two hundred and seventy-six male goats, and twelve calves for redemption. All of these were sacrifices to the Lord.
They delivered the king’s orders to the royal administrators and the governors of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, and they honored the people and the Lord’s temple.
When these things had been completed, the leaders approached me and said:

The people of Israel, the leaders, the priests, and the Levites have not kept themselves separate from the foreign peoples of the land and their impurities—the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Moabites, and Egyptians.

For they and their sons had lived with those peoples’ daughters, and the holy offspring had become mixed with the foreign peoples of the land. The chief leaders and nobles had shared in this lawlessness from the beginning of the affair.
As soon as I heard these things, I tore my clothes and my priestly robe, pulled hair from my head and beard, and sat grieving and distressed.
All those who trembled at the word of the Lord, the God of Israel, gathered around me while I mourned over this lawlessness. I sat distressed until the evening sacrifice.
When I rose from fasting, with my clothes and priestly robe torn, I bent my knees and stretched out my hands toward the Lord, saying:
“Lord, I am ashamed and shrink from your presence.
“For our sins have become more numerous than the hairs on our heads, and our sins committed in ignorance reach up to heaven.”
Indeed, from the days of our ancestors until this day, we have been deeply sinful.

Because of our sins and those of our ancestors, we, together with our brothers, our kings, and our priests, were handed over to our kings, to the sword, captivity, and plunder, with shame, to this very day.
And now, relent, for a little mercy has come to us from you, Lord, leaving us a root and a name in the place of your sanctuary,
so that your light may be revealed in the house of the Lord our God, to give us sustenance during our slavery. Even while we were serving as slaves, we were not abandoned by the Lord,
Instead, he showed us kindness before the Persian kings, to give us sustenance.
and to glorify the temple of our Lord, to restore ruined Zion, and to give us security in Judea and Jerusalem.
And now, what can we say, Lord? Despite having these things, we have transgressed your commandments, which you gave through your servants the prophets, when you said,
“The land you are entering to inherit is a land defiled by the defilement of the foreign peoples of the land. With their uncleanness they have filled it with uncleanness.
Now do not settle their daughters with your sons, and do not give your daughters to their sons.
Never seek peace with them, so that you may grow strong, eat the good things of the land, and pass it on to your children forever.”
All these things that have happened to us have come because of our evil deeds, our evil sins, and these great sins. For you, Lord, have made light of our sins
and have given us such a root. Yet we turned again to transgress your law by mingling with the uncleanness of the peoples of the land.
Were you not angry with us, to destroy us until no root, offspring, or name of ours remained?
Lord of lords, God of Israel, you are faithful. A root has been left to us today.
Look, now we are before you in our lawlessness, for with these things we can no longer stand before you.

While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and lying on the ground before the temple, a very large crowd gathered around him from Jerusalem: men, women, young people, and children. For there was a great deal of weeping.

Jeconiah, who had come in from among the Israelites, cried out and said, “Ezra, we have sinned against the Lord and have brought foreign women from the people of the land to live with us. Yet now there is hope for Israel.
Because of these things, let us swear oaths to the Lord to send away all our foreign wives, together with their children, as you have decided.” And all those who obeyed the law of the Lord,
standing up, said to Ezra, “Get up and carry this out, for the matter is your responsibility, and we are with you. Be strong and act.”
Ezra stood up and made the heads of the families of the priests and Levites, and all the Israelites, swear to do these things. And they swore.
Ezra rose from the temple courtyard and went to the treasury chamber of Jonathan son of Eliashib.
He spent the night there, neither tasting bread nor drinking water, mourning over these great acts of lawlessness committed by the multitude.
A proclamation was made throughout Judea and Jerusalem to all those who had returned from captivity, ordering them to come to Jerusalem.

Anyone who did not appear within these two or three days, according to the decision of the elders and the leaders of the assembly, would have his livestock consecrated to the priests, and he himself would be excluded from the community of those who had returned from captivity.
All those from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin gathered in Jerusalem within three days. It was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month.
The whole multitude sat together in the temple passageways, trembling because wintry weather had set in.
Ezra stood up and said to them, “You have acted wickedly and brought foreign women to live with you, adding to Israel’s sins.”
Even now, give confession and praise to the Lord, the God of our ancestors,
and do his will. Separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from these foreign women.”
The multitude cried out and said in a loud voice, “We will do as you have said.”
“But the multitude is large, and it is the winter season. We cannot stand out in the open air. Nor is this a task we can finish in one or two days, for we have sinned greatly in these matters.
So let the chief leaders of the multitude take their places, and let all those from our settlements who have foreign wives come at appointed times.”
along with the elders and judges from each place, until the Lord’s anger over this matter is turned away.”
Jonathan son of Hazael and Jahzeiah son of Tokan accepted these arrangements. Moses, Jenaab, Levi, and Shabbethai acted as mediators among them.
Those who had returned from captivity acted in accordance with all these things.
And Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of their families, all designated by name. They sat down together on the new moon of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
And they brought these matters concerning the men who had married foreign women to a conclusion by the new moon of the first month.
Among the priests who had assembled, some were found to have foreign wives:
from the descendants of Jeshua son of Jozadak and from his brothers: Mattathias, Eleazar, Jorib, and Jonadab.
They pledged to send away their wives and to offer rams as atonement for their unwitting offense.
And from the descendants of Immer: Hananiah, Zebadiah, Mani, and Shemaiah. And from the descendants of Oman: Maaseiah, Maana, Shemaiah, Neriel, and Azariah.
From the descendants of Pashhur: Elhanan, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Cainirus, and Shaatha.
And from the Levites: Zabad, Shimei, and Kelaiah, who is Calitas, and Pethosh, Judah, and Jonah.
And from the priestly singers: Eliashib the firstborn.
And from the daughters of Shallum and Toblan.
From Israel: from the descendants of Parosh: Jeremiah, Jedaiah, Malchi, Michael, Eleazar, Hashabiah, and Benaiah.
From the descendants of Ulla, Mattaniah, and Zechariah: Azarel, Joadiah, Jeremoth, and Jedaiah.
And from the descendants of Tattum: Eliada, Elishama, Othniel, Tarimus, Shekathiah, and Zerdiah.
And from the descendants of Bebel: Johanan, Hananiah, Zechariah, and Hamathiah.
And from Benjamin: Olam, Malluch, Jedaiah, Jashub, Agilush, and Jeremoth.
And from the descendants of Addi: Nahathush, Basaus, Ismu, Sisael, Baanah, and Manasseh.
And from the sons of Hanan: Elionas, Aseas, Malchias, Sabbeus, Simon, [?].
And from the descendants of Hashum: Mattaniah, Mattanah, Benaiah, Eliphelet, Manasseh, and Shimei.

And from the descendants of Bani: Jeremiah, Moadash, Ishmael son of Almada, Peshiah, Hazo, Abizion, Eliteshua, Amtilimus, Elishish, Banus, Elishmish, Shelemiah, and Nethaniah. And from the descendants of Zerah: Shishi, Azbariah, Hazael, Shammoth, Zimri, and Joseph.
From the descendants of Nooma: Martiah, Zebadiah, Hadiah, Joathar, and Benaiah.
All these had women of foreign descent living with them, and they named them along with their children.
And the priests and Levites who were from Israel lived in Jerusalem on the new moon of the seventh month, and the Israelites lived in their own settlements.
And the whole assembly gathered together in the square to the east of the priestly threshold.
And they said to Ezra, the chief priest and reader, “Bring the law of Moses, which was given by the Lord, the God of Israel.”
And Ezra the chief priest brought the law before their entire assembly, both men and women, and all the priests, to hear the law on the new moon of the seventh month.
And he read in the square in front of the Priests’ Gate, from morning until noon, before the men and women. And the whole assembly paid attention to the law.
And Ezra, the priest and reader of the Law, stood on the wooden platform that had been prepared.
And with him on the right stood Mattathias, Shammua, Hananiah, Azariah, Uriah, Hezekiah, and Baalshamush.
And on the left: Paldana, Mishael, Malchiah, Dutha, Tasub, Nabralash, and Zechariah.
And Ezra took the book of the law before the assembly, for he was seated at the front in a place of honor before them all.
And when he opened the law, they all stood upright. And Ezra blessed the Lord Most High, ruler of all.
And all the people cried out, “Amen, amen!” And after raising their hands upward, they fell to the ground and worshiped the Lord.

Jeshua, Benaiah, Sherebiah, Neraaniah, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maana, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hananiah, and Phaethus, the Levites, were teaching the law of the Lord. They read the law of the Lord to the assembly, while they were inspired together, and for the reading [?].
And Aphrates spoke to Ezra, the chief priest and reader, and to the Levites who were instructing the assembly in everything.
This day is holy to the Lord, and they were all weeping when they heard the Law.
“Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to those who have nothing.
For the day is holy to the Lord. Do not be distressed, for the Lord will glorify you.”
And the Levites were instructing the whole assembly, saying, “This day is holy. Do not be distressed.”
And they all went to eat and drink and enjoy themselves, to send portions to those who had nothing, and to rejoice greatly.

For they had been inspired by these words that they had learned. And they gathered together. This book too is finished, namely the first book of Ezra. Because we did not find it in the Peshitta text, we copied it according to the Septuagint.
